definitions.explanation: A person who loves to eat and always wants to eat a lot. While it can mean glutton, it is often used affectionately or playfully, especially when referring to children or pets.

examples.english: Our dog is a big eater.

examples.japanese: {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}な⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦おやつ→おやつ：17921_oyatsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦ねだっている→ねだる：07619_nedaru⟧。
examples.english: A greedy child is begging for snacks.

examples.japanese: {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦にとって→にとって：06803_nitotte⟧、⟦{旅行|りょこう}→旅行：00748_ryokou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一番|いちばん}→一番：01140_ichiban⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{楽|たの}しみ→楽しみ：01651_tanoshimi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{地元|じもと}→地元：09941_jimoto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧ことだ。
examples.english: For a foodie like me, the best part of traveling is eating the local cuisine.

notes:
USAGE:
{食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう} has a playful, affectionate tone and is not strongly negative. It is commonly used for children and pets, or self-deprecatingly. The na-adjective form {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}な is also used as a modifier. The word {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}⟦{万歳|ばんざい}→万歳：04339_banzai⟧ was the title of a long-running TV cooking show.

SIMILAR WORDS:
⟦{大食|おおぐ}い→大食い：08341_oogui⟧ (big eater) and ⟦{食|た}べ{過|す}ぎ→食べ過ぎ：28819_tabesugi⟧ (overeating) focus on quantity, while {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう} emphasizes the love of eating itself.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}な⟦{子|こ}→子：09851_ko⟧ (greedy child)
- {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{猫|ねこ}→猫：02237_neko⟧ (greedy cat)
- {食|く}いしん{坊|ぼう}⟦{万歳|ばんざい}→万歳：04339_banzai⟧ (name of a famous TV show)
